title: OpenAI releases model-generated science claims for external scrutiny
dek: The lab is testing different validation and publication methods for mathematical, complexity and physics results produced by AI.
evidence: OpenAI's announcement of research claims; independent validation incomplete
takeaway: Separate model-generated proof artifacts from verified scientific conclusions; invest in reproducibility and expert review.

sections.title: Three distinct cases

bullets.detail: OpenAI published a claimed harmonic-analysis result and associated artifacts so outside researchers can study the argument.
A claimed result involving the Exponential Time Hypothesis is being examined with an external expert group; a claimed physics result is following a different, initially withheld-artifact review path.

paragraphs: Mathematics: OpenAI published a claimed harmonic-analysis result and associated artifacts so outside researchers can study the argument.

Complexity: A claimed result involving the Exponential Time Hypothesis is being examined with an external expert group; a claimed physics result is following a different, initially withheld-artifact review path.

sections.title: What matters

bullets.detail: A formal-looking proof or model-generated manuscript is not equivalent to independent acceptance of a major theorem. Different disciplines require distinct validation processes.
Treat formal checks, reproducible experiments, external critical review and provenance as separate validation gates. Publish uncertainty at the same prominence as the claim.

paragraphs: Verification gap: A formal-looking proof or model-generated manuscript is not equivalent to independent acceptance of a major theorem. Different disciplines require distinct validation processes.
Engineering insight: Treat formal checks, reproducible experiments, external critical review and provenance as separate validation gates. Publish uncertainty at the same prominence as the claim.
